observation.visible_scene: A top-down view of a CD/DVD disc set into a black circular ring resting on a white surface, forming a clock-like face. Gold/orange handwritten numerals are already on the ring: an upside-down '12' at the bottom and a '9' on the right. A left hand grips a brown squeeze bottle with a yellow label and a fine tip (marker/glue applicator), pressing the tip against the ring at the lower-left position (around the 11 o'clock spot). A right hand's fingers hold the ring steady at the upper-right. The disc shows a bright vertical rainbow reflection band through its center.
visible_changes: The left hand keeps the applicator tip in contact with the black ring at the lower-left, drawing/laying down a small gold stroke there; the mark near the tip grows slightly from a tiny dot into a short '1'-like/arrow stroke over the sequence.
The left hand and bottle shift position modestly (drifting a little up and left) while the tip stays on the same region of the ring.
The right hand and the disc remain essentially stationary, holding the assembly in place.
The disc's rainbow reflection band and the existing '12' and '9' numerals stay in the same orientation throughout.
The framing wobbles slightly (small camera jitter/rotation) but the scene composition is largely unchanged.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the bottle actually contains and whether ink is flowing is not confirmable.
The identity of the numeral being written (e.g., '11' vs '1') and the start/finish of the writing action are outside this excerpt.
Earlier and later positions of the hands and any further numbers on the ring are not shown.
uncertain_details: Whether the small positional drift of the left hand is intentional drawing motion or camera movement is ambiguous; the tip's contact with the ring is the reliable cue.
The exact shape of the new gold mark is hard to resolve at this resolution.
